title: Vesper and the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1917, Sebastian Voss, a battlefield nurse who secretly records in his ledger the names of soldiers erased from official reports, receives a letter written in the unmistakable hand of Lieutenant Edmund Hale — a man officially listed as dead. The letter leads him to a riverside workshop where Hale, disfigured and hiding under a false name, is racing to complete an inheritance: a set of commissioned instruments meant for a family that believes him buried. As ice groans on the river and military police close in on deserters, Sebastian must choose between returning the ledger's truth to the record and protecting the living man behind it. They finish the work as the river breaks; Hale surrenders himself to face charges, but Sebastian's ledger — entered into evidence — secures his pardon, and the two begin a new life carrying far less than they once did.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing field hospital records from the First World War. She writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. In a freezing casualty clearing station, Sebastian tends the wounded and records in his private notebook the names officers omit from reports. The emotional beat is quiet defiance — he measures dignity in what can be carried, and tonight he carries thirty-one names.

chapters.title: A Letter from the Dead
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A Red Cross parcel contains a letter addressed to him in the handwriting of Lieutenant Edmund Hale, whom Sebastian personally recorded as dead eight months ago. The letter names a workshop on the Marne and pleads: before the ice breaks. Shock hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Leave of Absence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian bargains with Matron for three days' leave by volunteering for a supply run that passes near the river. The beat is risk disguised as errand; he hides the ledger sewn into his coat lining.

chapters.title: The Workshop on the Water
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He finds a half-flooded boathouse workshop and a scarred stranger called 'Mr. Ferris' who moves like a soldier and flinches at his own name. Recognition is mutual and terrible. The beat is the vertigo of meeting a ghost.

chapters.title: What Edmund Carried Back
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV (first use). Burned at a forward post he was ordered to hold, Hale deserted rather than die nameless; the army listed him dead to save paperwork. Now he owes a death-debt: finishing his late father's commissioned instruments. Shame drives every scene.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The will requires completion and delivery by spring thaw or the estate passes to a cousin who will sell it all. Edmund shows Sebastian the unfinished work — delicate mechanisms needing steady nurse's hands. A bargain forms: help me, and I'll tell you every omitted name.

chapters.title: Thirty-One Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Over candlelight, Edmund confirms men from Sebastian's ledger, including Private Doyle, whose mother still waits. Sebastian realizes the ledger could clear Edmund — or hang him. The beat is the weight of paper as both weapon and mercy.

chapters.title: The Cousin Arrives
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ambrose Hale appears at the village inn, sniffing after the inheritance, charming and cold. He nearly crosses paths with Edmund at the chandler's. Tension spikes; Edmund learns the thaw is early this year.

chapters.title: Hands That Remember
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Working side by side, their rhythms sync — his precision, her... his patience. Sebastian teaches Edmund to eat again without pain; Edmund teaches him lathe-work. The beat is tenderness arriving uninvited between two men trained not to want.

chapters.title: Patrol on the Ice Road
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Military police sweep the river villages for deserters. Edmund hides beneath floorboards while boots cross above; Sebastian lies smoothly for the first time in his life. Afterward they cannot stop shaking, or holding on.

chapters.title: Ambrose Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ambrose confronts Sebastian, having guessed 'Ferris' is Hale, and offers him money to walk away — or be reported as a deserter's accomplice. Sebastian refuses. The beat is duty inverted: which uniform serves the living?

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confesses the full truth: he wrote to Sebastian deliberately, having seen the nurse's name in a comrade's dying words. He chose Sebastian because he knew he'd come. Anger, then understanding — being chosen was its own kind of rescue.

chapters.title: Doyle's Mother
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A letter arrives from Mrs. Doyle asking if anyone remembers her son. Sebastian writes back the whole truth, first entry ever sent outward. The beat is grief made useful; the ledger begins turning inside out.

chapters.title: Cracks in the River
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The final instrument — a music box mechanism for Edmund's dead sister — resists completion; his burned hand fails him. Despair nearly breaks him until Sebastian guides his fingers through it. Intimacy becomes explicit in all but word.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Inn
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A drunk stable boy sells Edmund's location to Ambrose, who summons the provost marshal. Sebastian discovers the betrayal too late; the beat is dread compressing time — two days until delivery, one day until arrest.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They pack the finished instruments into instrument cases small enough to carry, abandoning everything else. Edmund wants to run; Sebastian argues surrender with the ledger as defense. Their first real fight — love against duty, each claiming the other's side.

chapters.title: The Delivery
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At dawn they deliver the instruments to the family solicitor just as the provost's men reach the workshop. The will is honored; Ambrose is left with nothing but his name. The beat is triumph shadowed by the knock coming up the path.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund surrenders voluntarily, asking only that Sebastian keep the ledger safe. Handcuffed on the ice road, he looks back once. The emotional beat is terrible calm — a man finally wearing his true name.

chapters.title: The Ledger Entered
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At the hearing, Sebastian testifies and submits the ledger: thirty-one omitted names, corroborated by survivors, proving Edmund's wounds were sustained holding a position he was ordered to abandon-or-die. The room goes quiet page by page.

chapters.title: Verdict Before the Thaw
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Pardon granted on grounds of mistaken death record; the army prefers its paperwork corrected quietly. Edmund walks out into rain. The beat is anticlimax as grace — no trumpets, just a door opening.

chapters.title: Breaking Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The river cracks and shifts overnight; they watch the thaw from the repaired workshop window, the instruments gone, the debt paid. They speak plainly at last about what they are to each other. The beat is release.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue-tone. Spring: Sebastian keeps nursing but now sends every ledger entry to the families; Edmund teaches apprentices. Evening prayer-song gives the title its meaning — the light you work by when the day's duty ends. They carry little, and it is enough.
